intro.heading: Understanding Scheme Documents — SID, SAI & KIM
intro.subtitle: A Guide to Mutual Fund Offer Documents | Read Before Investing
intro.summaryLine: Innovate Securities Pvt. Ltd. | ARN-42505 | www.innovatesec.com | Last Updated: August 2026
intro.notice: SEBI regulations require Mutual Fund schemes to be accompanied by offer documents — typically the Scheme Information Document (SID) and Key Information Memorandum (KIM) for each scheme, together with the Statement of Additional Information (SAI), which is generally prepared at the Mutual Fund / AMC level and incorporated by reference into the SID. These documents contain risks, costs, objectives, and other material terms. Innovate Securities encourages investors to read the current documents for the relevant scheme and AMC before investing. Official copies are available from the AMC website, AMFI, and SEBI portals linked below.

blocks.heading: The Three Key Mutual Fund Documents

items.title: SID — Scheme Information Document
items.body: The primary scheme-specific document covering investment objective, risks, costs, asset allocation, and other scheme particulars. Read in conjunction with the SAI.

items.title: SAI — Statement of Additional Information
items.body: Generally an AMC / Mutual Fund–level document covering constitution, tax, legal, KYC, and other common information. It is typically not a separate scheme-by-scheme document and is incorporated by reference into the SID.

items.title: KIM — Key Information Memorandum
items.body: A concise scheme-specific summary of critical facts, often attached to or accompanying the application form. Use it as a quick reference, not a substitute for the SID and SAI.

blocks.heading: 1. Scheme Information Document (SID) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The SID is the primary legal document for a Mutual Fund scheme. A typical SID covers areas such as:
bullets: Investment Objective — for example growth, income, or a capital preservation objective, where specifically stated in the scheme documents, without assurance
Asset Allocation Pattern — equity, debt, derivatives, REITs, etc., as disclosed for the scheme
Risk Factors & SEBI Riskometer — market, credit, interest rate, liquidity and other disclosed risks; always check the scheme’s current Riskometer
Total Expense Ratio (TER) — Direct Plan and Regular Plan, as disclosed
Exit Load Structure — charges on early redemption, if applicable
Benchmark Index — as specified for the scheme
Fund Manager Details — as disclosed in the SID
Historical NAV / performance information — where disclosed
Dividend / IDCW information — where applicable
Minimum Investment Amounts — lumpsum, SIP, additional purchase, as disclosed
Redemption & Settlement — timelines and cut-off times, as disclosed
Fundamental Attributes — core characteristics that may require investor consent to change

blocks.heading: 2. Statement of Additional Information (SAI) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The SAI generally contains Mutual Fund / AMC–level information that applies across schemes of that fund house. It is usually not issued as a separate document for every individual scheme. Typical SAI content includes:
bullets: AMC & Trustee Company Details — CIN, address, board, key personnel
Sponsor Information
Rights of Unit Holders
Tax Treatment of MF Investments — as disclosed
KYC Requirements — FATCA/CRS, NRI norms, and related disclosures
Penalties & Pending Litigation against the AMC, where disclosed
Investor Grievance Mechanism and SEBI SCORES details
AML / KYC Policy of the AMC
Associate Transactions — related-party disclosures

blocks.heading: 3. Key Information Memorandum (KIM) — In Detail
blocks.intro: The KIM is a scheme-specific summary document often attached to or used with the Mutual Fund application form. Typical KIM content includes:
bullets: Investment Objective (summary)
Asset Allocation Table
SEBI Riskometer — as currently disclosed for the scheme
NAV information — Direct and Regular Plans, where shown
Benchmark Index and Fund Manager Name, where disclosed
Exit Load and Minimum Investment Amounts, where applicable
Plans Available — Direct Plan and Regular Plan
IDCW option details, where applicable
Standard Mutual Fund risk disclaimer

blocks.heading: Understanding the SEBI Riskometer
blocks.intro: SEBI requires Mutual Fund schemes to disclose a Riskometer label. Do not assume a fixed risk level for an entire category such as overnight, large-cap, or small-cap funds. Risk labels can differ between schemes in the same category and can change over time based on portfolio composition. Always check the current Riskometer of the specific scheme in its latest SID / KIM / AMC disclosure before investing.
bullets: Low
Low to Moderate
Moderate
Moderately High
High
Very High

blocks.body: The Riskometer is updated by AMCs based on portfolio composition. Always verify the current Riskometer for the specific scheme before investing. Regulatory reference: SEBI circulars / guidelines on Mutual Fund Riskometer disclosures.

blocks.heading: Where to Get These Documents
bullets: AMC Official Website — Investor / Downloads / Scheme Documents / SID-SAI-KIM section for the specific scheme and fund house
AMFI Portal — portal.amfiindia.com for scheme and related offer documents
SEBI Website — sebi.gov.in for Mutual Fund regulatory disclosures and guidance
MF Central — mfcentral.com for investor account and related services
Application Form — KIM is often attached to or accompanied by the physical / digital application form

Innovate Securities can also help you locate the current official SID / SAI / KIM for a scheme — email Mfinnovate@gmail.com or call +91 98795 06993. Prefer downloading from the AMC / AMFI / SEBI sources above so you always use the latest version.

items.title: Know Your Risks
items.body: Review the scheme’s risk factors and current Riskometer. Do not rely on category assumptions — check the specific scheme documents.

items.title: Know Your Costs
items.body: TER, exit load, and other charges are disclosed in the scheme documents. Higher costs can reduce net returns over time.

items.title: Check Suitability
items.body: The investment objective indicates whether the scheme is intended for goals such as wealth creation, income, or a capital preservation objective, where specifically stated in the scheme documents, without assurance.

items.title: Understand Lock-in
items.body: Some schemes have lock-in or fixed-maturity features (for example ELSS or certain close-ended schemes). Confirm liquidity terms in the scheme documents before investing.

items.title: Verify Fund Manager
items.body: Fund manager details and changes are disclosed in scheme documents. Review the SID for current information.

items.title: Compare Options
items.body: Reading KIMs and SIDs of similar schemes can help you compare TER, exit load, Riskometer, and other disclosed features before deciding.
